# Preparing for a Mountain Hike

Choosing the right trail depends on elevation gain and distance, not just the
summit altitude. A short trail with a steep ridge can be far harder than a
long trail with a gentle slope. Hikers should check the total elevation gain
before committing to a route, since altitude sickness can appear above two
thousand five hundred meters regardless of how fit the hiker is.

Footwear matters as much as route planning. Sturdy hiking boots with ankle
support protect against rolled ankles on loose alpine scree. Trail runners
are lighter and fine for well maintained paths, but a rocky ridge crossing
calls for a stiffer boot with a proper sole.

A well packed backpack keeps heavier items close to the back to preserve
balance on exposed ridgelines. Water, a map, an emergency shelter, and extra
layers are the core of any mountain packing list, since alpine weather can
shift from sun to storm within an hour near the summit.
